rows.question: Moonveil: đòn nhẹ và đòn nặng của Transient Moonlight khác nhau về hướng đánh và tầm ra sao?
rows.expected_answer: Đòn nhẹ quét ngang có projectile tầm ngắn; đòn nặng bổ dọc có projectile tầm trung. Không suy các con số damage hiện tại.

response.answer: Đòn nhẹ của Transient Moonlight là một cú quét kèm sóng ánh sáng tầm ngắn, còn đòn nặng là cú chém từ trên xuống với sóng tầm trung, nên đòn nặng vươn xa hơn rõ rệt [1]. Đòn nhẹ thường nhanh hơn và quét rộng hơn, trong khi đòn nặng đánh một mục tiêu và khó lăn tránh thẳng ra sau hơn; dù vậy, cả kỹ năng vẫn hiệu quả nhất ở cự ly cận chiến vì lúc đó cả lưỡi kiếm lẫn sóng phép đều có thể trúng [1].

sources.title: Moonveil
sources.text:
The Unique Skill: Transient Moonlight is the regular Skill: Unsheathe but with added projectiles: a short-ranged one for the light attack sweep and a mid-ranged one for the heavy attack overhead slash.
The skill is useful in roughly the same ways that Unsheathe is, meaning that the light attack follow-up is generally slightly quicker and much wider in exchange for being slightly weaker, while the heavy attack follow-up hits a single target slightly harder and is slightly more difficult to roll directly away from.
One stark difference is that the different attacks are much less dissimilar, with the light attack follow-up having less of a damage difference (22% less for Unsheathe, 10% less for Transient Moonlight) and much less of a Stance damage difference (50% less for Unsheathe, 8% less for Transient Moonlight).
While this does give the weapon some more reach (though mostly with the heavy attack follow-up), the skill is still the most effective at melee range since that means both the weapon and the magic waves can hit the target.
The skill's heavy attack follow-up has a weird interaction with jumping players and deals a lot less damage against them for some reason.
While a hybrid Intelligence/Dexterity build gains the highest total Attack Power a pure Intelligence build only loses about 2% total Attack Power in exchange for the skill's projectiles getting 13% higher Attack Power, making the latter generally preferable.

local_evidence_context.title: Moonveil requirements
local_evidence_context.text: Moonveil's listed one-handed requirements are Strength 12, Dexterity 18 and Intelligence 23. Requirements are distinct from scaling, recommended stats and damage; this does not establish latest-patch damage.

local_evidence_context.title: Unique Skill: Transient Moonlight
local_evidence_context.text:
The base Magic Attack Power of the magic projectiles scale with user Intelligence and weapon upgrade level.
The scaling is greatly increased by Moonveil's default Intelligence-scaling.
The Attack Power (AP) for the light attack follow-up's magic projectile is always at least 560 for a weapon at maximum upgrade level, while for the strong attack follow-up's projectile it's always at least 620 for the same situation.
At +10 and with 23 Intelligence the magic wave's Attack Power is 821 for the light attack version and 908 for the strong attack version, with 45 Intelligence it's 1004 AP and 1111 AP respectively, and with 80 Intelligence it's 1135 AP and 1257 AP respectively.
Both follow-up attacks can be parried, and the waves of light can be spell-parried.

local_evidence_context.title: Unique Skill: Transient Moonlight
local_evidence_context.text:
The light attack follow-up slash deals 450% of the weapon's base Stance damage, while the wave of light deals 100% of the weapon's base Stance damage. The strong attack follow-up deals 450% of the weapon's base Stance damage, while the wave of light deals 150% of the weapon's base Stance damage.
As Moonveil is a Katana, the light attack follow-up deals 22.5 points of Stance damage with the slash and 5 points of Stance damage with the wave of light, while the strong attack follow-up deals 22.5 points of Stance damage with the slash and 7.5 points of Stance damage with the wave of light.
In PvP, the light attack follow-up deals 1215% of the weapon's base Poise damage, while the wave of light deals 270% of the weapon's base Poise damage. The strong attack follow-up deals 1215% of the weapon's base Poise damage, while the wave of light deals 405% of the weapon's base Poise damage.
Both the light attack follow-up and the strong attack follow-up inflict 100% of the weapon's Status Effect build-up. This does not apply to the waves of light.
Both the light attack follow-up and the strong attack follow-up deal 100% of the weapon's Weapon Buff Attack Power. This does not apply to the waves of light.
The light attack follow-up slash has a Damage Level value of 2 (Moderate Stagger) while the wave of light has a Damage Level value of 3 (Long Stagger). The strong attack follow-up slash has a Damage Level value of 3 (Long Stagger), while the wave of light has a Damage Level value of 3 (Long Stagger).

rows.question: Does the stat spread 40 Vigor, 20 Mind, 20 Endurance, 12 Strength, 18 Dexterity, 53 Intelligence, 8 Faith and 8 Arcane match level 100 by the sum-minus-79 rule?
rows.expected_answer: The sum is 179, so it matches level 100 arithmetically. This does not prove optimality, damage or weapon eligibility.

response.answer: Yes — that spread adds up to 179, and with the level rule (sum of the eight attributes minus 79) that comes out to level 100 [1].

sources.title: Attribute point accounting
sources.text: A character's level equals the sum of the eight primary attributes minus 79. Thus the target attribute sum is level + 79. Vigor affects HP; Mind affects FP; Endurance affects stamina and equip load. Arithmetic does not establish optimality.

retrieval_queries.query: Does the stat spread 40 Vigor, 20 Mind, 20 Endurance, 12 Strength, 18 Dexterity, 53 Intelligence, 8 Faith and 8 Arcane match level 100 by the sum-minus-79 rule?

local_evidence_context.title: Attribute point accounting
local_evidence_context.text: A character's level equals the sum of the eight primary attributes minus 79. Thus the target attribute sum is level + 79. Vigor affects HP; Mind affects FP; Endurance affects stamina and equip load. Arithmetic does not establish optimality.

local_evidence_context.title: Greathood
local_evidence_context.text:
Increases both Intelligence and Faith by 2, at the cost of a 9% HP penalty.
The large HP penalty generally makes this head piece not really worth it at more than 40 Vigor, complicated further by how late it can be acquired. Instead, a more focused head piece with a penalty to Stamina or FP is more worth it since those can generally be countered with less of a stat investment.
At 60 Vigor it will lower maximum health from 1900 to 1710, roughly the same amount of health as 50 Vigor. At 50 Vigor it will lower maximum health from 1704 to 1534, the same amount of health as 43 Vigor. At 40 Vigor it will lower maximum health from 1450 to 1305, the same amount of health as 37 Vigor.
Good alternatives are the Hierodas Glintstone Crown for +2 Intelligence (and +2 Endurance), as its FP penalty will always be outweighed if at or below the Mind softcap of 40, or the lightweight Ruler's Mask for +1 Faith and no penalty or the heavier Imp Head (Corpse) for +2 Faith (with an effective Equip Load penalty due to weighing 3 units more).
Large enough to lower the visibility around the wearer's head slightly, which can prove a problem.

local_evidence_context.title: Witch's Glintstone Crown
local_evidence_context.text:
Grants a +3 to both Intelligence and Arcane in exchange for a -18% to Stamina.
This Stamina penalty is generally effectively the same as a -6 to Endurance for the purpose calculating total Stamina when at 20 Endurance, or -18 when at 40 Endurance.
Overall no worth it due to the very large Stamina penalty, and because the combination of Intelligence and Arcane only really synergizes with the Albinauric Staff and Maternal Staff .

local_evidence_context.title: Lazuli Glintstone Crown
local_evidence_context.text:
Grants +3 to both Intelligence and Dexterity in exchange for a -18% to HP.
This HP penalty is effectively the same as a -4 to Vigor at 20 Vigor, a -6 to Vigor at 40 Vigor, and a -16 to Vigor at 60 Vigor.
While the bonus of this helmet is strong, the massive HP penalty makes it not really worth it even at low levels of Vigor and especially not at levels above 40.

local_evidence_context.title: Sword of St. Trina
local_evidence_context.text:
The skill, Mists of Slumber, is notable for being a strong tool for inflicting Sleep, both from the mist's 90 Sleep build-up per second and from the Weapon Buff it grants for 30 seconds, giving the sword another 20 Sleep build-up on top of its innate 66 Sleep build-up, 86 Sleep build-up total.
In combination with the innate Sleep build-up, a buffed Sword of St. Trina can make the notoriously strong-but-sleep-vulnerable Godskin Noble fall asleep in two hits. This is quite valuable since it is a very easily accessible and reusable tool for inflicting Sleep.
Gains the most Attack Power from a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build or a pure Dexterity build, while the Intelligence-scaling is largely useless due to being the weakest scaling (maxing out at 36% versus Strength's 50% and Dexterity's 72%) and scaling the much, much weaker Magic damage.
For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 542 AP, 80 Dexterity grants 533 AP, and 45 Dexterity and 45 Intelligence grants 490 AP.
While it can technically match the strongest Keen Straight Swords (Longsword and Broadsword) in terms of pure Attack Power, the fact that a considerable part of that is Magic damage (about 20% on a pure Dexterity build) hampers the damage a bit.
The Prisoner origin can wield the Sword of St. Trina immediately without having the level up any stats.

response.answer:
Moonveil yêu cầu một tay Strength 12, Dexterity 18 và Intelligence 23 [3]. Samurai khởi đầu với Str 12, Dex 15, Int 9, nên bạn đã đủ Str, chỉ cần thêm 3 Dex để chạm 18 và đẩy Int từ 9 lên 23 [5].

Với Transient Moonlight, hướng Int thuần chỉ mất khoảng 2% tổng Attack Power so với build lai Int/Dex, nhưng đổi lại sóng kiếm được cộng khoảng 13% lực, nên nhìn chung Int-heavy là lựa chọn tốt hơn cho PvE [2]. Vì vậy cứ giữ Dex đúng mức yêu cầu rồi dồn phần còn lại vào Intelligence.

Ở level 100, tổng tám chỉ số của bạn là 179 điểm [4]. Trừ phần tối thiểu cho yêu cầu vũ khí, phần lớn nên chia cho Vigor, một ít Mind và Endurance vừa đủ mặc giáp/né, rồi đổ vào Int — đây là hướng gợi ý chứ không phải một con số tối ưu đã kiểm chứng.

Mình chưa thể xác nhận quy tắc respec nên không đưa ra bảng tám chỉ số chính xác; nếu bạn nói rõ có được đổi chỉ số tự do hay không, mình siết con số cụ thể hơn.
